subject: Reserved pool top-up pricing and throughput guarantees — renewal conversation
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@oztech.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@oztech.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved pool top-up pricing for renewal

Hi Kimberly —

We’re coming up on our annual renewal with Redwood and the usage has ramped faster than expected. Current committed pool (8x A100-equivalent) is trending to hit sustained saturation during business hours. We’re evaluating either: (A) adding a block of reserved GPUs to the existing pool, or (B) resizing to a 12x pool.

Couple of asks to move the internal approval forward:
- A ballpark incremental monthly cost for +4 A100-equivalent GPUs vs full resize to 12x (committed pricing, 12-month term).
- Any step changes to throughput guarantees or latency SLOs if we switch to a larger pool.
- Whether a mid-term top-up can be added to current committed contract or requires an amendment with different discount tiers.

Would prefer to have numbers for our finance and procurement review by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Infrastructure
OzTech AI
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@oztech.ai>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@oztech.ai>, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-02T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved pool top-up pricing for renewal

Alex —

Appreciate the heads-up. I attached an initial quote and a simple capacity model that compares "+4 GPU block" vs "resize to 12x" on a 12-month reserved term. High level:

- +4 GPU block (attached as a top-up amendment): ~ $28,000/mo (committed unit price), equivalent to ~22% blended discount vs on-demand. No immediate SLA step-change — throughput scales with pool size, but sustained tail latency SLOs are posture-dependent (we recommend increased prefetch and batching for peak windows).
- Resize to 12x committed pool: ~ $32,500/mo (lower per-GPU rate because of larger commit), includes a 30% discount band and a 30-day SLA credit table at the 99.5% latency P95 target for API calls.

Key commercial notes:
- Mid-term top-ups are supported and show up as an amendment to the existing contract. They lock the new GPUs into the current commit term length; discount tier is prorated monthly.
- A full resize (move to 12x) is cleaner operationally and gives slightly better unit economics but requires an amendment and a technical migration window (we can make this near-zero downtime with rolling placement).

Attachments: RDW_OzTech_TopUp_Quote_v1.pdf, capacity_modeling.xlsx

If helpful I can propose two formal options (A & B) and add a small conditional discount if you sign amendment + 12-month extension today (I put a placeholder in the quote).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-02T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: OzTech top-up pricing — discount flexibility

Kimberly — quick internal note before you finalize.

- We can offer a one-time commercial uplift: if they commit to +4 now and extend the term to 18 months (total), we can move pricing from $28k/mo -> $24k/mo for the incremental block (effectively additional 14% concession).
- For a resize to 12x, legal prefers an amendment with updated SLA table; sales ops can prepare standard amendment + migration helper.
- For throughput guarantees: product requests 30% headroom target on KV cache & batching to guarantee P95 SLAs. If OzTech can share a 48-hour peak token profile we can confirm precise SLO numbers.

Recommend you hold the conditional 18-month concession in the offer if procurement is hesitant.

Marcus
Director, Commercial Strategy
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@oztech.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@oztech.ai>, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-03T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved pool top-up pricing for renewal

Thanks Kimberly — and thanks Marcus for the internal note.

A few quick clarifications from procurement before we loop legal:
1) If we take the +4 block with the 18-month concession, can you confirm if the top-up is billed pro-rata for the first month? We’ll be aligning to our fiscal month.
2) For the resize option: you mentioned a 30% discount band. Can you confirm whether this is a guaranteed floor during the 12-month term or if it’s dependent on usage thresholds?
3) SLA credits: we need a clear SLA credit schedule for latency breaches (P95) tied to monthly spend. Procurement will want that in the amendment.

If you can send a short one-page summary that we can share with finance/legal (costs, billing proration, SLA credit table), we’ll aim to get an LOI by Friday.

—Alex
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@oztech.ai>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@oztech.ai>, marcus_lin@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved pool top-up pricing for renewal

Alex —

Quick one-pager attached and I’ve summarized below for you to share with finance/legal:

1) Billing/proration: top-up blocks are billed pro-rata from the amendment effective date to your billing cycle; then full month renews on your regular invoice date. We’ll add a one-time invoice note to help procurement reconcile.

2) Discount mechanics: the 30% discount band on a 12x commit is a committed price (floor) for the 12-month term — it is not usage-contingent once signed. The +4 block has the blended discount described earlier; the conditional 18-month concession (to $24k/mo for the incremental block) requires an 18-month lock on the incremental capacity.

3) SLA credits: attached table in the one-pager (and clause proposed in updated_amendment_draft.docx). Example: if monthly P95 latency exceeds target by >25% for more than two non-consecutive days, we apply a % credit based on monthly committed spend (tiered: 2% / 5% / 10%). Legal can tweak thresholds but we prefer a simple tiered schedule.

Next steps I suggest:
- If procurement is comfortable, sign the amendment (DocuSign link below) for the +4 block with 18-month concession so we can provision within 7 business days.
- If they prefer resize to 12x, sign the 12-month resize amendment and we’ll schedule a short migration window.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abcd-oztech-topup
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Attachments: RDW_OzTech_TopUp_Quote_v1.pdf, capacity_modeling.xlsx, updated_amendment_draft.docx

Let me know if you want me to loop in our legal to a call with OzTech legal — happy to set a time.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
